headline: Task-specific DNA and RNA language models encode biological constraints
label: Task Specific Genomic Language Models
summary: Recent preprints and one published study pair nucleic acid language models with pretraining domains, conditioning, or functional oracles for specific tasks.
synthesis: The shared thread is explicit encoding of biological constraints into nucleic acid language models, rather than reuse of generic embeddings. GPN, pretrained on 455 apicomplexan assemblies, improves epigenomic prediction in Plasmodium falciparum. MARRI couples pretrained RNA foundation model representations with opening penalties and hybridization gains in cross-RNA attention. B-RANKO, a 150M-parameter bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA model, supports both sequence generation and representation learning. GenNA conditions nucleotide generation on natural-language annotations across 2221 eukaryotic species. GENECraft and REGAL pair sequence models with functional oracles to design controllable regulatory DNA and tissue-specific enhancers. The items are heterogeneous in modality and goal; the dominant thread is specialization rather than a single method.
